name: Deep Soft Bluish Violet
lede: Deep Soft Bluish Violet is a muted, darkened reading of [[violet]] pulled toward blue, from Ridgway's 1912 plates and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system.

sections.title: Three words doing specific work
sections.body:
The name layers *deep* (lower lightness), *soft* (lower chroma) and *bluish* (a hue shift) onto the base color [[violet]], in the library's own modifier grammar [1]. Ridgway's 1912 plate XXIII, hue 57′, tone i, is the recorded source, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 later filed the same chip into block 207, named strong violet in that system's own list [1].

Its closest look-alike is [[dauphin-s-violet]], about 3.3 units off, with [[deep-soft-blue-violet]] close behind at 3.4 [2]. [[foxglove]] and [[blanc-s-violet]] sit further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.03% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (8 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 2 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 82% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 100% of its 2 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1658, 254 years before the name's 1912 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
